facts.text: The constructor opens the serial port with rtscts=0, xonxoff=0 and timeout=0
The constructor initializes every arm with PI, SP0 and SA and every pump with Z1 0 R
armaddr is [18, 28] for the two arms and pumpaddr is [11] for the syringe pump
Move formats the arm command PA x y z, sends it to armaddr[armnum-1] and stores the position in curpos
MoveAxis formats the command XA, YA or ZA with an integer position and updates curpos
AddPosition stores coordinates [x, y, z] under a name in locations
ShowPosition returns the stored curpos of an arm
Draw takes bottle or sample as source, refuses a draw above 2000 units of syringe content and calls Pump twice
Dispense refuses more units than the tracked syringe content and calls Pump twice
Pump refuses a speed below 0 or above 20, a position below 0 or above 2000, and a direction other than in or out, then sends S<speed> A<position> <I|O> R
The protocol frames each message as 0xFF 0x02 <message> 0x03 <checksum> 0x0D
The protocol lists PI, SP0, SA and PA for arms and Sx Ay d R for syringe pumps, with no stop or halt command
The protocol addresses arm 1 as 18, arm 2 as 28, syringe 1 as 11 and syringe 2 as 12
The protocol return codes are @ accepted, A error, Q execution in progress and Y finished
The README describes a library and GUI for Waters 2700-compatible liquid handlers with 1-2 arms, attached syringes and one 6-port valve
The README lists moving up to two arms and drawing or dispensing with the syringe pump and 6-port valve
The example calls Move, AddPosition, Goto, Draw and Dispense

safe_state.description: none: the protocol documents no stop or halt command, so a moving arm cannot be stopped, and a zero-speed Pump command is outside the protocol's 1-20 speed range (the model review blocked the package, RESULT.json)
